mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 4% over the next month reduces the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows, lowering the present value of expected dividends and earnings, which drives a negative S&P 500 forward return over the following 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by 0.25% in the next month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative despite the FEDFUNDS increase, or the effect size is statistically insignificant (p > 0.05 in a regression controlling for FEDFUNDS).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in unemployment benefits (PAYEMS) reduces aggregate demand, while a concurrent decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals weak manufacturing momentum; together, these dual signals predict a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls by > 2,000 while INDPRO falls by > 5% in the same month
regime_hint: labor market easing combined with weak manufacturing
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.01) when the interaction signal is active.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% in the next month suggests the Fed is less likely to raise rates, lowering risk premiums and pushing up S&P 500 forward returns over the following 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by 0.3% in the next month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite CPIAUCSL falling below 2%, or the effect is not statistically detectable (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and retail sales (not in catalog, so use GDPC1 as proxy for demand which can reflect weak overall activity) over two months indicates a supply-side contraction that reduces growth expectations, producing a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for two consecutive months and GDPC1 falls by 2% over the same period
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive and robust across multiple rolling windows (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 0.2 percentage points, it often precedes a pause or cut in Federal Reserve policy rates, which lowers the cost of capital and supports higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by > 0.2% in the next month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative or flat despite the UNRATE increase, with a t-statistic below -1.5 in a regression.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in housing starts (not in catalog, so use HOUST proxy as a labor-demand indicator) above historical averages in the next quarter suggests stronger labor absorption and optimistic business outlook, driving a positive S&P 500 forward return over 60 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by 10% over the next quarter
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative and the effect is not captured in a Granger causality test (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in both manufacturing (INDPRO) and consumer demand proxies (e.g., GDPC1) for two consecutive months create a supply-demand imbalance that depresses growth expectations, resulting in a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO down 2% and GDPC1 down 1% in the same month, repeated the following month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) when the interaction signal is present.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (indicated by rising FEDFUNDS), the S&P 500 anticipates future rate path through a forward discounting channel, producing a negative 20-day forward return as investors price in lower equity valuations.
regime_hint: initiation or continuation of a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative and the discounting effect is not detected in a Fama-MacBeth regression (p > 0.10).
